passage: It was the week after the singing competition, when Francis's voice cracked on the high note. At lunch, the boys at the corner table kept doing the crack, a squeak and then laughter, every time Francis walked past. I didn't want to make a speech. I'm not good at those, and speeches make things louder. So I just picked up my tray and sat down across from Francis, like I always had. I asked about the cricket score. Francis answered in a low voice, staring at the dal. The squeaks came twice more, then stopped. Maybe they got bored. Maybe it's less fun when the person isn't alone. Walking back to class, Francis said, "Thanks, Samir." I said, "For what? You still owe me the score." We both knew for what.

qa.q: What happened to Francis's voice at the singing competition?
qa.a: Francis's voice cracked on the high note.

qa.q: Why did Samir choose not to make a speech to the corner table?
qa.a: Samir felt awkward about speeches, which make things louder, and wanted to back Francis quietly instead.

qa.q: Which small choice made the difference at lunch?
qa.a: Sitting across from Francis as usual and talking about cricket, so Francis wasn't alone and the mocking lost its audience.

qa.q: What might "Thanks, Samir" tell us about how lunch felt for Francis?
qa.a: Francis was likely embarrassed by the squeaks but grateful not to face them alone, even though nothing was said out loud.

grounding: A student sees a classmate mocked at lunch and quietly sits with them instead of lecturing the mockers, and the teasing fades.

passage:
PE teacher's note, Class 9, Tuesday
During the relay, Ganga tripped at the handover and fell. A group near the stands started chanting "Ganga-flop" and filming on a phone. Before I reached them, Tushar had jogged over, offered Ganga a hand up, and walked with her to the water tap. He didn't say a word to the group, just stood beside her while she rinsed her grazed knee. The chanting fizzled out within a minute; there was no one left to perform for.
What I did next: I checked Ganga's knee and sent her to the sick room with Tushar. I spoke to the group about the chanting and had the video deleted in front of me. I've informed the class teacher and will call Ganga's parents this evening. I also told Tushar privately that I saw what he did.

qa.q: What did the group near the stands start chanting?
qa.a: "Ganga-flop."

qa.q: Why do you think Tushar said nothing to the group?
qa.a: He seemed to want to help Ganga rather than start a fight, trusting that standing beside her would matter more.

qa.q: Which of the teacher's follow-up steps protect Ganga most?
qa.a: Having the video deleted stops it spreading, and telling the class teacher and her parents means adults can keep watching out for her.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ganga to have Tushar beside her at the tap?
qa.a: Ganga may have felt less alone and less humiliated, able to rinse her knee without facing the chanting by herself.

grounding: A teacher records how a student quietly helped a mocked classmate away from the chanting without confronting the group, and what the teacher did next.
